sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Musa balbisiana is a large tropical Asian herb with a pseudostem about 6 m tall, formed by leaf sheaths. It is an ancestor of cultivated bananas. Unlike Musa acuminata, wild fruits are angular and contain large, hard seeds.

sections.title: Leaves, inflorescence and fruit
sections.text: The leaves can reach about 2.9 × 0.9 m and the pendulous inflorescence about 2.5 m. The angular, grey-green fruits are about 13 × 4 cm and contain many hard seeds 5–10 mm across.

sections.title: Use and edibility
sections.text: Wild fruits are very seedy. Kew reports that the male flower bud is eaten in Southeast Asia after soaking in salt water and cooking; this does not mean that wild fruits are table bananas.
